market_view: VIX 17.7 after a 20-day rise; the Fed hiked unanimously, yet yields dipped and tech led a higher close as oil eased. Oil remains elevated but the Saudi outage is read as less disruptive than feared.

oil_gas.catalyst: Continuing the existing XOM long on the Saudi pipeline supply shock; WTI 102.43 and Brent 105.83 still far above the exit level (~90). CNBC: 'Oil finishes the week flat as the market sees Saudi pipeline outage as less disruptive than feared'.
oil_gas.reasoning: Thesis is weaker today: oil fell 3% and XOM fell 3.5%, but WTI is still above 100 and no credible de-escalation is named. XOM lags crude, so some catch-up is possible. Marginal hold to about 09-28; exit if WTI nears 90.

gold_miners.reasoning: Newmont analyst target raises and a gold rebound are already priced. Gold is below its 200-day average, the 10-year yield is about 5% and the Fed just hiked. No unpriced catalyst.

chips.catalyst: none (CNBC: 'Jensen Huang says Nvidia will sell twice as many chips next year' is a management claim and likely priced; the AI rebound is mood)
chips.reasoning: Semis ETF is down 18% in 60 days with the AI-slowdown storyline unresolved. The Huang comment is not a checkable one-sided event, and general mood is not a catalyst.

pharma.reasoning: Headlines are policy background (Medicaid pricing, FDA newsletter). The breast cancer approval is not an LLY-specific item. No named catalyst.

copper_uranium.catalyst: none for FCX (the Niger uranium investment and Cameco offtake headlines concern CCJ, not the leader)
copper_uranium.reasoning: Copper is down 5.5% over 5 days with no FCX-specific news. The uranium headlines are not about the leader and are mostly priced.

would_change_my_mind: A credible Saudi or Iran de-escalation or WTI below about 90 would end the XOM long; a named, unpriced catalyst in another family would justify a long there.

handoff.what_changed: Fed hiked rates unanimously; yields dipped and tech rallied. WTI fell 3.2% to 102.43 and XOM fell 3.5%, with CNBC reporting the Saudi pipeline outage is seen as less disruptive than feared, which weakens the oil thesis.

oil_gas.position: long XOM since 2026-08-31, extended to about 2026-09-28
oil_gas.why: WTI still above 100 and no credible de-escalation, but the shock is seen as less disruptive and confidence is only marginal.

gold_miners.why: Gold is below its 200-day average, yields are near 5% and the Fed hiked; no unpriced catalyst.

chips.why: Huang's sales claim and the AI rebound are mood, not a checkable unpriced catalyst.

pharma.why: No LLY-specific catalyst in the headlines.

copper_uranium.why: No FCX-specific catalyst; uranium news concerns CCJ.

open_storylines.name: Iran war, Saudi strikes and oil
open_storylines.note: WTI 102, but the pipeline outage is seen as less disruptive than feared; exit XOM about 2026-09-28, on credible de-escalation, or if WTI falls toward 90.

open_storylines.name: Fed hike and yields
open_storylines.note: First hike in years under Warsh; 10-year about 5.0% but dipping; watch the first-Friday jobs report and gold below its 200-day average.

open_storylines.name: AI slowdown warning and chip rebound
open_storylines.note: Chips rebounding on Huang's twice-the-chips claim, but semis ETF is down 18% in 60 days; long only on a clear unpriced catalyst.

open_storylines.note: US $414M Niger uranium deal and a Cameco laser enrichment offtake; relevant to CCJ, not the FCX leader; check for FCX-specific news.

handoff.next_job: Next decision day: read this note and the new record; hold XOM to about 2026-09-28 only while WTI stays well above 90 with no credible de-escalation, and exit on de-escalation or WTI near 90; stay flat on the other families unless a named, unpriced catalyst appears; watch yields, the Fed and the jobs report.
